title: Porygon Is Code That Cannot Be Copied
premise: Porygon consists entirely of programming code, yet its copy protection prevents duplication.
audiencePromise: Follow Porygon from digital data to the strange rule that keeps one copy from becoming two.
openLoop: How can a Pokémon made of code refuse to be copied?
payoff: Porygon can enter cyberspace as program data, but copy protection keeps copying from making another Porygon.
engagementQuestion: Is that brilliant security, or a strange contradiction?

voice.instructions: Speak quickly and clearly with curious disbelief. Pause briefly before each reveal, then land the final either-or question warmly.

scenes.headline: CODE THAT CANNOT BE COPIED
scenes.narration: Porygon is made of code, yet copying cannot duplicate it.
scenes.caption: CODED, BUT NOT COPYABLE

scenes.headline: ITS BODY BECOMES DATA
scenes.narration: Its body can revert to program data and enter cyberspace.
scenes.caption: POKÉMON → PROGRAM DATA

scenes.headline: PORYGON IS COPY-PROTECTED
scenes.narration: But the Pokédex says Porygon is copy-protected against duplication.
scenes.caption: COPYING IS BLOCKED

scenes.headline: THE SECOND COPY FAILS
scenes.narration: So copying the code does not create a second Porygon.
scenes.caption: CLONE FAILED

scenes.headline: DIGITAL, BUT STILL ONE
scenes.narration: Copying still fails, even though Porygon is entirely code.
scenes.caption: CODE DOESN'T MEAN CLONES

scenes.headline: BRILLIANT OR CONTRADICTORY?
scenes.narration: Is that brilliant security, or a strange contradiction?
scenes.caption: SECURITY OR CONTRADICTION?
